# dsh-openrouter-sync
Keep the DSH `openrouter` provider model list in sync with OpenRouter's currently-free models.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin,
packaged as a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and

`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `openrouter-sync` row into the active profile.
Host-only plugin: eve
ry six hours it rewrites the `openrouter` provider models in the active profile patch; HMR recompose
rs it rewrites the `openrouter` provider models in the active profile patch; HMR recomposes it live.
## Install

- Desktop app: **Plugins** → install `github:bosenok/dsh-openrouter-sync` (private repository:
give

the machine git access), then enable the bundle.
- CLI: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:b

osenok/dsh-openrouter-sync`.
- Local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:/path/to/dsh

ter-sync`.
- Local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:/path/to/dsh-openrouter-sync`.

Enabling the bundle mounts the plugin; HMR applies it to a running app, and a
restart makes sure the
client half is rebuilt.

> Note for the app-managed `desktop` profile: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add`
> only installs the

dependency and copies the package; unlike a regular profile
> it does not enable the bundle. Enable

it by adding the package name to
> `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`

(or through the
> Plugins page). Other profiles enable the installed bundle automatically.
## Where the key comes from

The host half resolves `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` through the harness credential
service first, then the p

rocess environment, then
`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`; with no key it still lists the provider's model

s only
when configured — the sync itself is skipped. Nothing plugin-specific to set up
beyond the Op

enRouter provider (or an `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` entry in the
credential store / environment layers).
